SpeederProto · render comparison · 7 Sep 2026

Which look parameters add, and which detract

Each variant was captured on the same scripted drive (steer bias left, so the split takes the tunnel). The demo now runs on a fixed timestep, so each pair is the identical frame of the identical run and the parameter is the only difference. Drag the divider across each pair; the left side is always the baseline. All of these are live in the HUD under Look variants.

keep as optionundecideddetracts

Reference · baseline settings

Obstacles

Hologram barriers

keep as option
obstacleSkin = 1 · translucent magenta panel, 42 % opacity, emissive frame

Reads instantly at any distance because it is the only saturated magenta slab on the road, and the see-through panel keeps the road visible behind it. It also fits the fiction of a security cordon. Downside: magenta is already the lane-dash colour, so on the busiest stretches it can merge with the markings. Your pick from the first sheet, and it holds up here.

BaselineHologram barriers

Downtown, second block · t = 6 s · drag the divider (or use ← →); same frame of the same scripted run

Obstacles

Neon wireframe crates

undecided
obstacleSkin = 2 · twelve orange edges, dark core

Airy and stylish up close, but thin edges lose contrast against the lit facades and vanish under bloom at 60 m or more. Best kept as a secondary type for near-field clutter rather than the main hazard.

BaselineNeon wireframe crates

Downtown, second block · t = 6 s · drag the divider (or use ← →); same frame of the same scripted run

Atmosphere

Thin fog

detracts
fogLevel = 0 · density 0.0020 per m (baseline 0.0060)

Everything stays crisp to the horizon, which exposes the repetition of the segments and flattens depth. The far city reads as a wall of dots instead of receding.

BaselineThin fog

Downtown, second block · t = 6 s · drag the divider (or use ← →); same frame of the same scripted run

Atmosphere

Thick fog

keep as option
fogLevel = 2 · density 0.0140 per m

Strongest sense of distance and it hides the recycling completely, at the cost of the far skyline. Good candidate for the tunnel branch or a weather change; a touch heavy as the permanent default.

BaselineThick fog

Downtown, second block · t = 6 s · drag the divider (or use ← →); same frame of the same scripted run

Post pass

Low bloom

keep as option
bloomLevel = 0 · 0.5× bloom, bright threshold 0.84 (baseline 1×, 0.74)

Cleanest read of the road and obstacles. Neon looks like lit plastic rather than glowing gas, so some atmosphere goes with it. Worth pairing with thick fog if readability wins.

BaselineLow bloom

Downtown, second block · t = 6 s · drag the divider (or use ← →); same frame of the same scripted run

Post pass

High bloom

detracts
bloomLevel = 2 · 2× bloom, bright threshold 0.56

Halos fatten every line and the lane markings start to bleed into the road. This is the overcrowding you noticed earlier; it also costs the most on the phone.

BaselineHigh bloom

Downtown, second block · t = 6 s · drag the divider (or use ← →); same frame of the same scripted run

Buildings

Bright windows

undecided
windowsBright · facade emissive 3.2 (baseline 1.0)

Facades come forward and the city feels more inhabited, but the windows now compete with signage and obstacles for attention and the bloom picks them up. A halfway value (about 2×) is probably the sweet spot.

BaselineBright windows

Downtown, second block · t = 6 s · drag the divider (or use ← →); same frame of the same scripted run

Buildings

Dense city

keep as option
secondRow + storefronts + bright windows

The fullest skyline: no black gaps between towers and the ground floor is alive. Entity count is the highest of the set, so it is the one to profile on the phone.

BaselineDense city

Downtown, second block · t = 6 s · drag the divider (or use ← →); same frame of the same scripted run

Buildings

Sparse city

detracts
secondRow off · storefronts off · every other near tower removed

Sky shows between the towers and the base of the buildings goes dead, which reads as unfinished rather than quiet. The second row and the storefront strips are doing real work.

BaselineSparse city

Downtown, second block · t = 6 s · drag the divider (or use ← →); same frame of the same scripted run

Tunnel

Dense tunnel rings

keep as option
tunnelDense · white ring every 4 m between the coloured 8 m rings

Doubles the strobe rate of the tunnel, which sells speed and gives the eye a rhythm to steer by. Slightly busier at low speed; ideal when boosting.

BaselineDense tunnel rings

Undercity tunnel · t = 9 s · drag the divider (or use ← →); same frame of the same scripted run

Wet road

No reflection pools

detracts
reflections off · fake decals under lights removed

The road turns matte and the neon stops touching the ground. The pools are cheap and they are most of the wet look.
